News.title: Jewel thieves jailed for 15 years after nicking £225,000 of gems in smash & grab with sledgehammer
News.content:
THREE balaclava-clad thugs who carried out a brazen daylight smash-and-grab at a family jeweller and stole £225,000 worth of gems have been caged.

Trio Deniz Mehmet, 28, Lee Ramsey, 46, and Robert Clarke, 50, targeted Gregory & Co jewellers in Richmond, south west London, on January 31.



They admitted conspiracy to rob and were each sentenced tor five years and three months at Kingston Crown Court yesterday (July 30).

The combined sentences total 15 years and nine months behind bars.



Shocking footage of the raid – which later went viral – showed the gang relentlessly battering their way into the family-run shop.

Witnesses watched in horror as one robber repeatedly hammered at the large front window until the glass finally gave way.



Another stood by clutching a large blue Ikea bag before the pair stuffed it with watches, bracelets and other jewellery from the smashed display.

Brave members of staff desperately tried to fend off the gang but were unable to stop them.

The thieves then fled on foot as stunned shoppers looked on, fearing for their own safety.

The robbery happened in Richmond, the picturesque London suburb where hit TV comedy Ted Lasso is filmed.

Detectives from the Met’s Flying Squad launched a major investigation, trawling through CCTV, carrying out forensic examinations and recovering a vehicle believed to be linked to the raid.



Their enquiries led officers to identify Mehmet, Ramsey and Clarke, who were arrested during a series of raids in Essex in March and April.

Body-worn camera footage released by police showed officers storming Ramsey’s home in the early hours of March 31 before handcuffing him.

Clarke was arrested after officers woke him while he was in bed during the same operation.



Mehmet was later detained while walking along a street in Basildon on April 8.

The three men, from Rochford, Harlow and Basildon respectively, all pleaded guilty to conspiracy to rob.

Despite the convictions, none of the stolen jewellery has ever been recovered.

Detective Superintendent Dan Mitchell, from the Met’s Flying Squad, said: “Robberies of this kind cause real concern for residents and businesses in the communities that are targeted. It’s they who feel the immediate impact.

“These sentences mark a significant step in what has been a detailed and determined investigation.



“I hope they demonstrate our commitment to tackling smash-and-grab robberies in London by going after those involved, wherever they are.

“The groups responsible should be under no illusion – we will pursue you relentlessly and hold you to account.”

The family-run jeweller, which has served Richmond for more than 45 years, previously thanked the public for rallying behind the business following the raid.

A spokesman for Gregory & Co said: “We’re a local, independent, family jewellers and have been in Richmond for more than 45 years.

“The public response to this incident has been overwhelming and we are grateful for the support and kindness we’ve received.



“We are reassured that overall, good outweighs the bad.”

News.title: Spain mobilises army as stores & bars close after thousands of migrants storm border and at least 18 die on trip
News.content:
SPAIN has mobilised its army after thousands of migrants stormed a border crossing, sparking terrified locals to close stores, restaurants and bars.

At least 18 people have died while trying to swim to Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in northern Africa that is seeing waves of migrants arriving on its shores.



Authorities urged the government to declare a national emergency as overwhelmed border guards struggled to deal with the influx.

It has prompted Madrid to mobilise army units to support the overrun Guardia Civil – who are still dealing with migrants arriving at nightfall.





Tanks and soldiers have been pictured taking the streets as they shut down to the border to Morocco.

Spanish President Pedro Sanchez is also due to visit the embattled enclave later today.



Local business owners opted to keep their shutters down as thousands flood the city centre.

Residents are reportedly fearing for their safety amid a high risk of looting and riots.

The President of Ceuta, Juan Jesus Vivas, was quick to declare a total humanitarian and social emergency.

He said: “In the past few days more than 1,500 migrants, both adults and minors, have come to Ceuta by sea.



“The reception centres are saturated – there is no more room for anyone in them and according to yesterday’s figures the number of people entering is more than 200 a day.”

Spain’s soft-touch Supreme Court has come under fire for ruling that migrants who arrive by sea should not be subject to immediate expulsion as they are not crossing a physical land border.

The decision has been exploited by people-smuggling gangs and brought with it a wave of undocumented migration.

In response, Italian PM Giorgia Meloni declared she is prepared to ban Spain from the Schengen area.



She wrote on X: “The images coming from Ceuta are striking and demonstrate, once again, that uncontrolled illegal immigration poses a concrete threat to the security of Europe’s borders.

“We are convening the relevant bodies, and following these meetings, we are prepared to intervene with extraordinary measures to defend the borders and the safety of citizens, including the suspension of the Schengen Area with Spain.

“On illegal immigration, we will not yield an inch: defending the borders, stopping human traffickers, and ensuring effective repatriations will continue to be the line of this Government.”



Spain‘s socialist government stands out for its pro-migration stance.

It has recently launched a scheme to provide legal status to 500,000 undocumented migrants and received a huge influx of applications.

Shocking video from yesterday’s explosion of arrivals in Ceuta showed crowds of people, mainly Moroccans, rushing across the sand attempting to make it to the road.

The majority are young men but several whole families, including young children, can also be seen.

They had managed to jump over the border fence separating the city from Morocco, according to Spanish state news agency EFE.



Some could be heard chanting “Viva Espana!” – Long Live Spain – as they walked past.

The Moroccan government also promised it would work “faithfully and permanently with Spain” in regards to the ongoing crisis.

They said: “Moroccan security forces are preventing the arrival of numerous people who are trying to reach Ceuta from Morocco.”

Morocco and Spain have reportedly agreed to return migrants who entered Ceuta during the latest surge, according to Hespress.

Vivas said 60 bodies had been recovered at sea in recent months with several washing up to shore in Ceuta.



He has warned the humanitarian crisis will only worsen while migrant centers are so full as hundreds of people will be forced to sleep on the streets.

He added that housing units for minors were now operating at 2,400 per cent capacity.

Back in 2021, 8,000 migrants swam from Morocco into Ceuta over a few days.

The arrivals also included the largest ever number of migrants in a single day, thought to be around 6,000.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ceuta residents had locked themselves indoors as the army rounded up migrants fleeing Morocco, La Vanguardia reported.



Hundreds of migrants risk injuries or even death every year while trying to jump over fences, hide inside vehicles or by swimming around breakwaters that extend into the Mediterranean Sea.

News.title: Famous mountain climber who starred in Netflix doc & has MBE goes missing after massive avalanche atop peak
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

ICE HORROR Famous mountain climber who starred in Netflix doc & has MBE goes missing after massive avalanche atop peak

A WORLD-famous mountaineer who starred in a hit Netflix documentary has gone missing after a huge avalanche tore through one of the world’s tallest peaks.

Nirmal Purja MBE, known as Nimsdai, is among ten climbers missing after the avalanche struck Pakistan’s Broad Peak on Thursday afternoon.



The 43-year-old former Royal Marine was leading a team on the 26,414ft mountain – the world’s 12th highest – when disaster hit.

The Alpine Club of Pakistan said the group has been out of contact for several hours as a desperate search and rescue mission gets under way.





Five Nepalese climbers, led by Purja, and Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, from Hunza, are among those believed to have vanished.

Rescuers are racing to reach the remote mountainside as officials scramble to deploy helicopters and other emergency resources.



Major General Irfan Arshad, president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, said the organisation was working closely with government officials to coordinate the rescue effort.

He said every effort was being made to send helicopters and other available relief resources to the area as quickly as possible.

Broad Peak stands 8,051 metres above sea level and is regarded as one of the toughest mountains in the world to climb.

Purja is one of the world’s best-known mountaineers.

He shot to global fame after climbing all 14 of the world’s mountains higher than 8,000 metres in just 189 days, smashing the previous record.



The astonishing feat was documented in the Netflix film “14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible”.

Before becoming a professional climber, Purja served for six years in the elite Gurkha regiment before spending a decade with the UK’s Special Boat Service.

In 2018, he was awarded an MBE by Queen Elizabeth II for exceptional military service in high-risk environments.

The search for Purja and the other missing climbers remains ongoing.

News.title: Hiker mauled to death by 13ft alligator had teeth marks on her shoulder bones as monster almost tore arm off
News.content:
THE autopsy of a hiker mauled to death by a 13ft alligator has revealed the beast’s teeth left marks on her bones.

The attack that killed Brittany Clark, 31, was so savage that one arm was almost completely ripped off while the other was left barely attached.



Clark died after being attacked while visiting Little Big Econ State Forest in Central Florida with her boyfriend and roommate on June 28.

Associate Medical Examiner Jenaye L. Mack carried out the post-mortem in Orlando the following morning.



The report concluded Clark died from “multiple blunt force injuries of the upper extremities”.

Mack wrote Clark suffered a “near complete traumatic amputation of the left arm at the shoulder and near complete traumatic amputation of the right distal forearm”.



The report also revealed bite marks on her left clavicle, left scapula and the front of her left arm.

Following the fatal attack, wildlife officers tracked down and killed the 13ft alligator nearby.



The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) later confirmed the slain animal was responsible for the attack using DNA.

Construction worker Brittany had been cooling off in the river with her boyfriend, Chance Allison, and roommate Jayden Hernandez when disaster struck.

Her desperate partner fought to wrench her free as the monster clamped its jaws around her.

The reptile then dragged her into a savage “death roll” while their dogs barked from the riverbank in a desperate attempt to fend it off.

Alligators and crocodiles use the violent spinning technique to overpower prey before drowning them.



Chance managed to free one of Brittany’s arms “for a moment” before the alligator clamped down on the other.

A chilling 911 call captured the horror as Hernandez screamed that Brittany’s injuries were “horrible”.

She told the operator: “One of her arms is completely off and the other one is like attached barely.”

She then pleaded: “Hurry… she’s losing a lot of blood… we need to stop the blood.”

Moments later, Chance shouted: “Both her arms, both her arms are off.”



When the operator asked where the other arm was, Hernandez simply replied: “Gone.”

Brittany survived the initial attack and was rushed to hospital but later died from her catastrophic injuries.

Her older brother, Nick, remembered her as “an amazing person” who was always willing to help others.

He said: “She was an amazing person. She was nice and helpful with anyone that needed any kind of help.”

Barr Street Trailhead, where the attack happened, remains closed until further notice.



The tragedy came amid a string of alligator attacks across Central Florida.

Just 24 hours earlier, a boy was bitten on the hand while fishing with his father, according to WESH.

Officials later euthanised the 8ft alligator believed to have been responsible.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

On June 21, a snorkeller was also bitten in Rainbow River, around 100 miles from where Brittany was fatally attacked.

Florida has recorded more than 450 alligator attacks since 1948, with just 30 proving fatal.

News.title: Tragedy as search is called off for Brit surfing star, 28, who vanished while paddle boarding in Portugal
News.content:
SURFER HORROR Tragedy as search is called off for Brit surfing star, 28, who vanished while paddle boarding in Portugal

A RESCUE operation has been called off after a talented Brit surfer went missing while paddle boarding off the southern coast of Portugal.

Arran Strong, 28, was reported missing at around 11.30am on Monday morning near the scenic Arrifana resort, prompting emergency services to launch a search.



The surfing star – who grew up in Portugal – had been completing a 560-mile paddle boarding marathon with his friend, Jose Maria Pyrrait, when he suddenly vanished.

Jose recalled seeing his friend’s board “drifting about 100 metres away” while the pair were attempting to cross from Monte Celrigo Beach to Carrapeteira.



After alerting emergency services on land, Jose spent two and half hours searching for Arran, to no avail.

The operation was unfortunately hindered by dense fog and was paused overnight before it resumed on Tuesday morning.



The National Maritime Authority confirmed on Wednesday that the search has been called off, despite not recovering a body.

On its website, it said: “The search was called off early (on Wednesday) evening without the victim being located.



“According to available information, the young man disappeared at sea after running into trouble while attempting to cross from Monte Clerigo Beach to Carrapateira; the friend accompanying him was rescued by a nearby local fishing vessel, which also recovered the board the victim had been using.”

In a heartbreaking tribute, his friend Jose said: “Today was a day of irreparable loss and profound sadness.

“Arran Strong, who accompanied me during the stage between Zambujeira and Monte Clerigo, is no longer with us.”

He said that the two of them stopped off at the resort to take a drink and a few photos before setting off again.

After heading off in front of Arran, Jose said he then “stopped to wait” for him – only to look back and see an empty board.



“I paddled to it as fast as I could, dived over and over again looking for him, but we were in a very deep area, and visibility was extremely poor.

He then called his support partner immediately and alerted the rescue services, spending nearly two and a half hours searching for Arran.

He added: “He remains missing to this day and, sadly, there is virtually no chance that he is still alive.”

The pair had spent years training together, with Jose thinking of him “like a son”.

“Strangely enough, he always told me he would die young,” he said.



“Right now, I feel a deep pain. The only faint comfort is that he departed at sea, the place he loved most.”

Love Island star and childhood friend Laura Crane also paid a heartrending tribute to the surfing legend.

Sharing pictures online, she wrote: “My Magical Best Friend – This still doesn’t feel real and there there truly are no words that can quantify this loss.”

“All I know is our world will never be the same again.”

GB Surfing paid tribute to the gifted Brit, who was the highest-placed British male surfer at the 2024 and 2025 ISA World Surf Games.



“Beyond his performances in the water, Arran was a fantastic team-mate, respected competitor and a kind, generous presence whose passion for surfing left a lasting impression on everyone who had the privilege of knowing him,” he said.

“His passing is a devastating loss to our sport and the wider surfing community, and he will be greatly missed.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A source from the rescue operation said “all the information gathered so far points to the possibility he had a health issue while paddling”.

News.title: Burnham needs to stop trying to be cool… people want a PM who tackles big issues rather than shares Spotify playlists
News.content:
SHOULD politicians ever try to be cool? Our political leaders certainly seem to think so.

Andy Burnham is all about the cool, Northern vibes.



He has a dedicated teenage TikTok fandom that helped propel him to No10 by splicing together video footage of the new PM set to bubblegum pop songs.

He danced on stage to New Order’s True Faith when he was crowned Labour leader.



Burnham even took the odd day off ­politics to DJ at clubs in Manchester’s trendy Northern Quarter (although this was when he was Greater Manchester Mayor — not PM).

Britain’s new Prime Minister is — we are told — “lit, rizz, dank”.



And he is not the only politician on a mission to show he is cool.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski is more likely to be seen on stage at a rave than being interviewed on the Six O’Clock News.

Even Reform’s Nigel Farage is all about the ­TikTok likes, with 1.5million followers on the platform.

Increasingly, it feels like politics is just a vibe — and we are being asked to drink the Kool-Aid.



On the one hand, there is nothing ­particularly new about politicians trying to be a bit hip.

Remember Tony Blair having Noel ­Gallagher and a bunch of artists round for beers at No10 as he rode the Cool ­Britannia wave? Or Gordon Brown saying he liked the Arctic ­Monkeys?

But then that proves my point — there is a fine line between cool and cringe.

As one veteran Labour MP said to me the other day, “The thing is — us ­politicians just aren’t cool.”



And there’s the rub.

Our political class are, by definition, the men and women in grey suits.

The public wants to see them hard at work fixing the NHS and stopping the small boats — not spinning discs on a stage in Ibiza.

Maybe some of our politicians used to be cool, way back when at university, when they had long, floppy hair, were in a band and wrote tortured poetry for their girlfriends.



But those are faded memories.

Once they cut off their locks, put on an M&S suit and took their first political internship they stopped being cool.

Instead, they stepped into a world of opening school fetes, judging the biggest marrow competition and shoving leaflets in people’s ­letterboxes.

It is important and often unglamorous work. But it is not cool.

Burnham became a ­parliamentary researcher for Labour MP Tessa Jowell when he was 24.



His life may have been a hedonistic whirlwind before — I really don’t know. But from that day on he joined the grind of politics.

Don’t get me wrong, politicians can and should be relatable. Even charismatic, if they can manage it.

They need to pass the “would I want to go for a pint with them?” test.

Farage and Burnham do. Turns out Keir Starmer didn’t — and that’s why he isn’t Prime Minister any more.

As countless Labour MPs tell me, ­Burnham just has better vibes.



But a word of warning to the new PM — cool vibes don’t last.

The British public want politicians who can run the economy, improve the NHS, and stop the small boats crisis.

They don’t really care what is on your Spotify jogging playlist or what your favourite IPA is.

And they don’t want to see you dancing in a club when the economy is in the ­doldrums and taxes are sky high.

Every time the Green Party throws a rave, it makes itself a little less electable and a little bit more fringe.



So, yes Andy, flutter those dark eyelashes at the TikTok camera as you pull a pint and tuck in to some scampi fries down the pub.

Incidentally, I love scampi fries and am always up for a TikTok collab.

But don’t chase the cool too hard. Listen to New Order at home and fix the boats crisis in public.

Then the voters will really rate you.

GREEN ZOE’S SHAMEFUL ‘ERROR’



A GREEN Party mayor wants to end her ­council’s link to Israel – on the third anniversary of the Hamas terror attacks.

Zoe Garbett, Mayor of Hackney in East London, has written to the city of Haifa in Israel saying she wants to end the twinning relationship and demanding a response by October 7.

This sounds like a sick joke. Unfortunately, it isn’t. October 7, 2023, was the date Hamas launched its bloody attacks on Israel.

Nearly 1,200 people were murdered, while thousands more were injured or kidnapped and held hostage.

It was the deadliest attack on Jews since the Holocaust.



Let that sink in.

Imagine choosing that date?

Garbett has apologised, describing it as an “oversight”, but surely no one is thick enough to pick it by ­mistake?

Regardless, what an insult to a country whose people were slaughtered by a Jew-hating ­terror group.

It is shameful.



FOR 70 years the Lovell ­Telescope has stood proudly in Cheshire – mapping galaxies far away and protecting us from the Soviets during the Cold War.

But now it is under threat and could close because of funding cuts.

Scientists are up in arms at the news, saying it damages the UK’s global reputation for research.

UK Research and Innovation has cut annual funding to Jodrell Bank, which houses the telescope, inset, by £2.8million, and now it is in a race against time to find the money to plug the shortfall.



Britain is a giant of science. We are the ­country of Isaac Newton, Charles Darwin and Stephen Hawking. We must not risk losing this reputation. The bureaucrats need to rethink the cuts.

BRITAIN is burning. Europe has been ablaze with wildfires for weeks, and now one has broken out in Suffolk.

The UK’s climate is changing. We are getting hotter and wetter, so why are we not building more reservoirs? Britain has not built a reservoir since 1992. That is nearly 35 years ago.

Our politicians are only too happy to set pie-in-the-sky Net Zero goals and spend billions buying solar panels from China.



But they can’t get their act together to build a single reservoir, which could be used to store water and put out a wildfire.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It is a dereliction of duty that shames every one of our political class. So, enough hot air about Net Zero.

Get on and do the day job – build the ­infrastructure we need.

News.title: ‘Intimidating’ female sailor who sexually assaulted 4 shipmates on Royal Navy warship to ‘dominate’ them is jailed
News.content:
NAVY ABUSE ‘Intimidating’ female sailor who sexually assaulted 4 shipmates on Royal Navy warship to ‘dominate’ them is jailed

A FEMALE sailor who sexually assaulted male and female colleagues while aboard a Royal Navy destroyer has been jailed.

Able Seaman Sian Dowsett, 25, was booted out of the Navy after being found guilty of abusing four colleagues in a “disgraceful” campaign of intimidation.



Dowsett was branded a “predator” by a military judge who heard how she targeted both male and female colleagues.

The court learned that Dowsett – who had “bisexual tendencies” – would “target new members” on board Type 45 destroyer HMS Dauntless.



She reportedly grabbed the male sailors by their crotches and stroked their arms on multiple occasions.

The suspect also allegedly made vastly inappropriate comments like, “I like my coffee how I like my men, big and strong”.



To make matters worse, she smacked female sailors’ bums and squeezed their breasts, saying, “Do you like that baby girl?”

A court martial earlier this year heard Dowsett took advantage of new recruits who she thought would not report her.



During the torrid proceedings, Dowsett was said to be a “cancer on the ship”.

One of her victims described the “embarrassment” of being molested by a woman of lower rank than her.

“I shared a mess with her and I couldn’t talk about the incident because she would hear,” the victim said.

“I was also embarrassed – not only that I had been sexually assaulted by a woman but a woman who was of a lower rank than me and who should look up to me.”

“She was an extremely intimidating character. She would scream and shout at people.



“I had so many sleepless nights when she was aboard. She had unrestricted access to me and I honestly believed she would physically attack me.

“I thought if she knew I reported it her anger would have been uncontrollable.”

One of her male victims told Bulford Military Court in Wiltshire how he was left feeling “anxious” after the harrowing ordeal.

“I felt guilty that I let it happen but I didn’t tell her to get off. I was assaulted again in the hangar,” he said.

“She did this to me in front of two males I work with which made me feel embarrassed. I stood there in disbelief.”



On top of the hefty jail sentence, she was dismissed from the Navy over six convictions for sexual assault.

Dowsett had reportedly been recently diagnosed with autism, which could cause “social exploitation, interpersonal misunderstanding and difficulty navigating social and institutional environments”.

Assistant Judge John Atwill said that these were “acts that any person would know are unacceptable”.

Sentencing Dowsett, the judge said: “Service personnel have little choice over who they work and live with. The confines of work in ships brings them into close proximity with work colleagues.

“The use of that proximity to abuse and dominate others violates their autonomy and drives division into the teams in which they work.



“Your behaviour towards them was disgraceful. You upset, frightened and disconcerted them and you had no regard for the impact of your behaviour.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You were a predator in that ship, and seemed to target newer members.”

Dowsett joined the Navy in 2019 and was serving as a chef aboard HMS Dauntless at the time of the offences.

News.title: Aunt of Brit woman found stuffed in suitcase pays tribute to ‘beautiful’ niece & says ‘we can’t believe this happened’
News.content:
THE aunt of a Brit woman found dead inside a suitcase has paid tribute to her “beautiful” niece and says: “we can’t believe this happened”.

Elisabeth Ross, known as Lisa, was discovered inside a suitcase by a homeless man in Athens on July 18, sparking a major police probe.



The 38-year-old was last seen leaving her friend’s house three days earlier on her way to see some American pals in the Kypseli district.

Cops tracing her final movements have said the Brit’s phone was switched on and being used in the days after she died.



They believe that messages were sent in an apparent attempt to mislead those who might have been trying to get in touch with her.

Her heartbroken dad revealed he had received haunting text messages from his daughter’s phone after her mysterious death.



The dad, a lawyer in Edinburgh, told Greek police he was sent several messages for two weeks after Lisa’s passing from a man now being viewed as the prime suspect.

Her aunt, Anne Bangham, has paid a touching tribute to her “beautiful loving” niece.

She wrote: “We just can’t believe it she was such a beautiful loving and kind young lady.

I wish I could get my hands on whoever did it. She had not long arrived there to work.



“It will take a while to sink in… We are absolutely devastated.”

Another woman wrote: “RIP beautiful Lisa. I will always remember you for your beautiful smile, warmth, care and kindness you showed to everyone.”

Lisa is believed to have travelled to Greece from the US for work via her hometown of Edinburgh.



She was reportedly staying at a friend’s house in Attica for several weeks before she was last seen on July 15.

Cops are desperate to uncover what happened to Elisabeth during the three days she is unaccounted for.

The homeless man who found her has insisted that the suitcase was not in the derelict building on July 16 and July 17.

His testimony has led police to believe her body was taken to the building on the evening of July 17 or the following morning.

They are now combing the area for security cameras that might have captured the suitcase dump.



Local hotels and residences are also being examined, with police speculating that the body was likely taken to the building from close quarters.

Police spokesperson Konstantia Dimoglidou told The Sun: “The key to this case is to find out what happened to the woman during those three days as we don’t know anything about her moves on the 15th, 16th and 17th.

“The main focus is to find her cause of death as the medical examiner did not find any signs of struggle or injury on her body.

“We are waiting for the toxicology reports to shed some light in the next few days.

“We cannot be talking about a murder if we don’t know what happened to her – maybe she died and someone tried to hide her body, anything is possible and at this point it’s too soon to tell.



“As part of the investigation we are also checking CCTV from the area where she was found and we are working to trace her phone.”

The exact date she died is still unknown, but the toxicology tests will help determine if foul play was involved.

A spokesperson for Greek police said: “No other evidence has emerged from the body or the suitcase that would allow us to identify another person.

“We are awaiting the result of toxicology tests to determine the cause of death, and ascertain whether foul play was involved.

“The investigation is ongoing.”



First Minister John Swinney said Ross’s family would be supported by the Scottish government and the Foreign and Commonwealth Office.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “This is an absolutely appalling case that has been reported overnight.

“And obviously I’m deeply concerned that such a tragedy has taken place.”

News.title: UK school opened in 1415 to close forever after 'financial challenge'
News.content:
UK school opened in 1415 to close forever after 'financial challenge'

The historic independent school will not reopen for next year due to 'financial challenge' after educating thousands of pupils since operating as a school

View 2 Images School blames 'financial challenges' for closure Stoke College in Stoke-by-Clare is set to close at the end of the summer term https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c932qdd82x8o

A historic UK school opened in 1415 closed at the end of this school year after 'financial challenge'.

‌



The independent school educated pupils aged between 11 and 18 for hundreds of years but will not reopen again.

‌



Stoke College, in Stoke-by-Clare, Suffolk was a fee-paying school that charged up to £19,662 a year for day students and £38,421 for boarding pupils.

‌



View 2 Images School blames 'financial challenges' for closure Stoke College in Stoke-by-Clare is set to close at the end of the summer term https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c932qdd82x8o

The historic site dates back through centuries of religious use, with it originating as a religious college in 1415 and operating as a school since 1954.

However, on July 22, 2026 liquidators were appointed, according to The Gazette.

‌



A statement from Stoke College said: "The school will not operate beyond the end of the summer term and does not intend to reopen for the 2026–27 academic year."

The school claimed that the introduction of VAT on school fees created financial pressure for the establishment.

This VAT was introduced by the government in order to help pay for more state school teachers in England.

‌



The news of its closure came as a shock to many as it was advertising for new admissions and held an open morning in May.

The latest publicly available financial documents for Cambridge Stoke College Ltd show an after-tax loss of £1.6m for 2024.

The school said that "the removal of business rates relief, rising employment costs and increasing operational expenditure" also added to its challenges.

‌



In November 2019 Stoke College was bought by new owners.

Announcing the closure, the school said: "The immediate priority is to support students, families and staff through this transition and to ensure continuity of education for every child."

Stoke College added that it would be working with nearby independent schools to help and secure spots for pupils.

‌



Principal Kim Terrar said: "This is an incredibly sad day for everyone connected with Stoke College.

"While we do not yet know what the future holds for this beautiful site, my focus now is on finding the best way forward for our incredible students and staff."

At its time of closure on July 1, the school taught 119 pupils according to Companies House.

Joe Whiley of Insolvency Direct Ltd has been appointed liquidator.

News.title: Suffolk fire live: Hundreds of firefighters battle 'unprecedented' wildfire near nuclear plant
News.content:
A wildfire is raging in Dunwich Heath, Suffolk where evacuations have been ordered - the blaze is close to three nuclear plant sites, and has burned an area the size of 210 football pitches

Hundreds of firefighters are battling through the night to contain a massive wildfire in Dunwich Heath, Suffolk, that has devasted a huge nature reserve and threatened a nearby nuclear power plant.

Temperatures soared into the mid-30s in southern England on Thursday, burning an area the size of 210 football pitches in a National Trust reserve just a few miles away from Sizewell B - the UK's largest nuclear power plant.

Some 200 caravans were evacuated this morning, with holidaymakers woken up by banging on their doors. Eighteen fire engines and more than 100 firefighters are now at the scene, with authorities saying they expect crews to be battling the blaze for the next two days.

There is also concern for wildlife in the area, after nature reserve RSPB Minsmere announcing its closure this morning. RSPB Suffolk area manager Adam Rowlands said the land was home to rare wildlife including nightjars - and it could take "more than a decade" for the habitat to recover.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the fire service will have “all of the support” they need in tackling the blaze.

On Thursday afternoon, an EDF spokesperson said the fire was “not affecting operations at Sizewell B power station”.

Have you been affected by the fire at Dunwich Heath? Get in touch with us at livenews@reachplc.com

News.title: Dunwich Heath fire: Couple recall 'frantic banging' on caravan door before escaping 'toxic fumes'
News.content:
Dunwich Heath fire: Couple recall 'frantic banging' on caravan door before escaping 'toxic fumes'

Stephen Bullock and his partner Christine Miller have described the moment they were awoken by "frantic banging" on their caravan door and managed to flee the scene

View 5 Images Stephen Bullock and his partner Christine Miller were evacuated from Dunwich Cliffs Estate caravan park (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

A couple from Essex have recalled how they escaped the Suffolk wildfire as they and hundreds of other caravan park guests were evacuated.

‌



Firefighters have been tackling the blaze in Dunwich Heath, near Leiston, since Wednesday evening, with more than a hundred firefighters and a helicopter on site. A major incident has been declared due to the size and complexity of the blaze - which at it's largest was 150 hectares – the equivalent of approximately 210 football pitches.

‌



Homes and 200 caravans have been evacuated. Residents were alerted by a 'hammering on the door' and told to evacuate immediately on Wednesday night.

‌



View 5 Images Although this remains a dynamic incident, the situation appears to be stabilizing (Image: Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service)

Donald Trump says Board of Peace reaches 'historic' agreement for Hamas to disarm in Gaza READ MORE :

Father-to-be plummets to death during freak accident while rock climbing READ MORE :

In an update last night the fire service said at least 12 fire engines will remain at the scene overnight into Friday in order to manage smaller fires that are breaking out, adding that electricity had returned to 111 of the 116 properties affected by earlier power cuts.

Suffolk Fire and Rescue service said Sizewell B nuclear power station was not at risk from the fire, due to the distance from the fire and the direction it was travelling, but said it was a "live and dynamic situation".

‌



Stephen and Christine's story

Stephen Bullock and his partner Christine Miller were staying at Dunwich Cliffs Estate caravan park, having travelled from Canvey Island in Essex for a three or four day stay. He became aware of smoke drifting across fields "quite a way away" at 5pm, which persisted for a few hours, then died down, so they watched a bit of TV and went to bed.

However, at 11pm there was "frantic banging" on the caravan door as the park warden was evacuating visitors, flashlight in hand.

He said: "It was pitch black. There were toxic fumes. You could not see your hand in front of your face. The fumes were horrific because it was quite a big fire by then and we were getting all of the smoke. We got in the car and put the headlights on, but it was thick black smoke everywhere. There were police and ambulance crews everywhere."

‌



View 5 Images Fire crews used a range of specialist equipment and resources to tackle the fire, including Unimogs, drones and 4x4 quad bikes. (Image: Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service)

The couple travelled to Westleton Village Hall where they were provided with the keys to a bungalow to stay the night. However, Mr Bullock said he did not know whether they would be returning to their caravan or returning to Canvey Island.

Another holiday maker Ed, from Epping in Essex, was staying at Dunwich Cliff. He could hear fire engines and said he subsequently received a memo from the campsite ordering people to evacuate, but said he made his own plans and drove to the Dunwich Tea Rooms where he slept in his car overnight.

‌



He said: "At 4am this morning, that whole area was red like a light and I personally thought the campsite must have gone up. There was so much red and fire, but the wind must have changed direction and it must have changed and it must have gone further towards the tea rooms away from the campsite."

View 5 Images The fire service were called to reports of a large wildfire at Dunwich Heath spreading rapidly south-west towards St James' Church, off Westleton Road. (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

Lisa Gordon and her husband's story

Lisa Gordon, 54, on holiday with her husband and dog in their touring caravan, evacuated from Cliff House Holiday Park on Wednesday night.

‌



Mrs Gordon told the Press Association: “Just looking at the pictures… it’s quite worrying how close it is to the park now. It’s a car, it’s a caravan, and it’s insured but at the end of the day it’s a lot of hassle, isn’t it? They are things that can be replaced. But it’s not the relaxing day we thought we’d be having.”

View 5 Images The helicopter is still in use, and will be available tomorrow. Each pass drops 1000 litres of seawater. (Image: Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service)

Article continues below

She said that when she and her husband were told to leave the holiday park, they could see smoke behind the trees.

Mrs Gordon added: “It was only as we walked to reception to meet the police that all of a sudden it kind of hit us. So where we were it didn’t seem too bad at all. We weren’t really panicking at all.

Follow our live blog for the latest updates on the Dunwich wildfire by clicking here.

News.title: Crete wildfires live: Rethymno in flames amid mass evacuations on Greek islands
News.content:
Flames are tearing across Greek Islands, forcing the evacuation of entire villages on Crete, Paros and Andros as wildfires continue to sweep across Europe

Raging wildfires have taken hold across several Greek islands, forcing villages to be evacuated as firefighters struggle to contain the flames.

Wildfires in the Rethymno region of the south of Crete are burning "out of control on all fronts", with firefighting aircraft unable to be deployed due to strong winds. Thousands of people, including tourists, were evacuated overnight. Urgent evacuation orders have also been issued for parts of Paros and Andros.

Three firefighters have died in Greece, with two becoming trapped in a vehicle while tackling the flames in Rethymno. Meanwhile, Europe's emergency response chief warned that the entire continent could be engulfed as wildfires rage in France, Spain and Portugal.

"Italy will face risk at the beginning of August, and we will need to see what will happen with the Iberian Peninsula, because if [it is] there as well, we will have all Europe on fire," Maria Zuber, head of the EU's Emergency Response Co-ordination Centre, said yesterday.

News.title: Police hope DNA evidence will snare 'Beast of Birkenhead' 40 years after brutal murder
News.content:
Police hope DNA evidence will snare 'Beast of Birkenhead' 40 years after brutal murder

Peter Sullivan then aged 30, was branded the “Beast of Birkenhead” when he was jailed for 38 years after being wrongly accused of beating florist Diane Sindall, 21, to death in August 1986

View 5 Images Florist Diane Sindall, 21, was beaten to death 40 years ago (Image: PA)

Detectives have DNA tested more than 600 men as they seek to solve a brutal 40-year-old murder for which an innocent man spent 38 years behind bars.

Peter Sullivan, then aged 30, was branded the “Beast of Birkenhead” and “Wolfman” after being wrongly accused of beating florist Diane Sindall, 21, to death in a frenzied sexual attack on August 2, 1986.

His conviction was quashed in May last year after he claimed he made a false confession following abuse by Merseyside officers. Now, ahead of the anniversary of the murder, the force has said they are doing “everything in our powers” to catch the killer.

‌



View 5 Images Peter Sullivan wrongly spent 38 years behind bars (Image: PA)

Inside Legacy funeral home of horrors where director Robert Bush left bodies piled up READ MORE :

Chilling last texts sent from phone of Brit woman found dead in suitcase in Athens READ MORE :

An investigation into the killing in the Wirral was relaunched in 2023 after DNA tests found a match for a male on samples taken from the scene. Extensive enquiries, including working with the National Crime Agency to identify the person the DNA profile belongs to, remains ongoing.

A Crimestoppers reward of up to £20,000 for information given exclusively to the charity that leads to the arrest and conviction of the person responsible for Diane’s murder remains in place.

Detective Superintendent Rachel Wilson, the officer leading the inquiry, said: “It’s unthinkable that 40 years on from Diane’s murder her killer has still not been brought to justice but I want her family, friends and the wider public to be reassured that we are doing everything in our powers to find that person.

“We have a dedicated investigation team who have been painstakingly reviewing the original investigation, re-interviewing witnesses, carrying out DNA tests and following up new information submitted by the public.

“We remain determined that Diane’s family get the answers they have waited so long for and that we get justice for Diane. Forty years is a long time but it is never too late for someone to do the right thing and come forward with any information they have which may help to assist our enquiries.”

‌



View 5 Images Memorial to Diane Sindall in Birkenhead (Image: Andrew Teebay Liverpool Echo)

She added: “In 1986 DNA was very much in the early stages and as such was not available to the detectives who originally investigated Diane’s death but her murder was fully investigated by the team.

“We believe the DNA profile will be key to finding the killer and to date have eliminated 575 people and 32 currently under review.

‌



“It is also possible that someone could hold information about the identity of Diane’s killer but either through fear or a misplaced sense of loyalty has not yet come forward. To those people I would say, please have the courage to tell us what you know.”

Diane was working part-time shifts at a pub in Bebington to help raise extra money for her planned wedding the following year. At the end of a Friday shift she set off for home, five miles away in Seacombe, in her blue Fiat van, only to run out of petrol.

View 5 Images Diane's blue Fiat van ran out of petrol

‌



She started to walk along a busy, well-lit main road and was spotted by witnesses walking along Borough Road towards Tranmere between midnight and 12.20am.

Twelve hours later Diane’s body was found by a dog walker in an alleyway. She had been beaten to death in a frenzied sex attack. According to police: “She had suffered extensive injuries to her body. Her cause of death was established as a cerebral haemorrhage following multiple blows.”

The murder prompted the biggest manhunt in the history of Merseyside police, with officers speaking to about 3,000 people. On 23 September, Sullivan was arrested after apparently giving police a number of different accounts of his movements.

‌



It was alleged that he had spent the day drinking heavily in a pub 10 minutes from where the body was found. After losing a darts match it was said Sullivan went out armed with a crowbar before what was a chance encounter with Diane.

View 5 Images Court drawing of Peter Sullivan as he finds out his conviction had been quashed (Image: Julia Quenzler / SWNS)

Sullivan was initially denied legal representation or an appropriate adult in police interview, on the grounds that officers were concerned that sensitive information might be leaked about the investigation.

‌



His trial in 1987 heard evidence from dental experts that bite marks on Diane’s body could be matched to Mr Sullivan’s teeth, leading to the ‘Wolfman’ nickname.

The DNA sample that secured his release was only made possible by a method that first came into use in 2015.

Speaking after his release Sullivan said: “I feel sorry for (Diane’s family), I really do feel sorry for them and what they’re going through at the moment, where they’re back at square one and not knowing who the person is that killed their daughter.

“I don't know what to say to them, I am really sorry for what's happened to their daughter, and if they need - if they want - my support when they go to court with the guy, when they find him, I will go to court with them, I will be there by their side 100%, because I will be there for them.”

News.title: Donald Trump says Board of Peace reaches 'historic' agreement for Hamas to disarm in Gaza
News.content:
Donald Trump says Board of Peace reaches 'historic' agreement for Hamas to disarm in Gaza

Donald Trump has said that Israeli forces will withdraw from Gaza, paving the way for a "new Palestinian government" to be established following a "historic agreement"

View 2 Images Trump threatened to revoke O'Donnell's U.S. citizenship in July 2025 (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump has announced his Board of Peace has reached a "historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza".

‌



Hamas is a Palestinian Islamist militant group and political movement. Founded in 1987, it has governed the Gaza Strip since 2007 and is designated as a terrorist organization by countries including the United States, United Kingdom, and Israel.

‌



The agreement marks a "critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government", President Trump said.

‌



View 2 Images Palestinians inspect the destruction following an Israeli airstrike in Al-Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

Donald Trump took to Truth Social to say: "Today, the Board of Peace reached a HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza. This is a monumental step toward lasting PEACE and SECURITY.

"This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people. At the same time, Israel will have the security it deserves, with Gaza no longer used as a base for terror attacks.

‌



"This is a major milestone in the implementation of the Trump 20-Point Plan. The agreement will be carried out in carefully structured phases. As disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will withdraw, and the International Stabilization Force will work with a new Palestinian police force to take responsibility for Gaza being safe for its residents and its neighbors.

"One year ago there was a violent raging war, humanitarian crisis and hostages kept in brutal captivity. We have made historic progress and there is still much work to do.

"I want to thank the mediators—Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye—for their important efforts, and especially my outstanding team, whose tireless work made this historic breakthrough possible.

Article continues below

"The threat that emerged from Gaza on October 7 will NOT be allowed to rebuild!

"Under this agreement, Gaza will finally be in the hands of a new Palestinian government that serves its PEOPLE. CONGRATULATIONS TO ALL ON THIS AMAZING DEVELOPMENT, THAT EVERYBODY SAID COULD NEVER BE ACHIEVED!"

News.title: Dating app rapist jailed after victims expose sickening pattern of abuse
News.content:
Dating app rapist jailed after victims expose sickening pattern of abuse

Muhammad Ans, 29, has been jailed for 20 years and placed on the sex offenders register for life after being convicted of raping three women he met on dating apps

View 2 Images Muhammad Ans has been jailed for his crimes (Image: Devon and Cornwall Police )

A serial rapist who attacked multiple women he met on dating apps has been jailed for 20 years.

‌



Muhammad Ans was convicted of four counts of rape against three women following a two-week trial at Plymouth Crown Court.

‌



The 29-year-old will also serve a further three years on extended licence and has been placed on the sex offenders register for life.

‌



Ans met his victims on various dating apps - Tinder, Bumble and Baddoo - between 2023 and 2025, the court heard.

One woman told police how after she was raped by Ans, he offered to pay her $3,000 in compensation if she would "leave it".

He began contacting the first woman on Bumble before arranging to meet in person near the end of 2023.

‌



The pair met and went out for a meal before Ans took the woman back to his accommodation in Coventry and raped her. He then went on to rape her again in a series of events in early 2024.

He messaged the victim again in August 2024 asking to meet up.

She confronted him about raping her over a number of messages, and he "apologised and offered to take her out shopping and to go for meals together". The woman refused.

‌



Days later, Ans met his second victim on the Baddoo app. By this time, he had moved to Tavistock and was living in a flat.

View 2 Images The sentencing was heard at Plymouth Crown Court (file) (Image: Carl Eve/PlymouthLive)

He messaged his second victim before meeting up with her in his car and taking her back to his flat, where they drank alcohol.

‌



The victim made it clear that she did not want to have sex, but Ans raped her.

Messages shown in court between Ans and his second victim show that after he dropped her home, she messaged him and challenged him about the rape.

Ans responded to his second victim by apologising, adding "that he couldn't stop himself".

‌



He offered to take his second victim shopping and claimed he wanted to get to know her and go to the beach with her. The victim refused and told him she was going to report him for raping her.

The same day, the victim reported Ans, and Detective Constable Craig Ferguson was appointed as the case officer, reports Plymouth Live.

Ans was identified, and his vehicle details were established by the police. A wanted appeal was issued for Ans, and he was located in Leeds after fleeing Tavistock.

‌



During an interview, Ans denied the offence, but admitted that he had met the victim. He claimed all sexual contact had been consensual and that his admissions in the messages were "confusion on his part despite his clear acknowledgement and apologies."

His phone was seized by police and taken for examination. Ans was bailed on conditions not to contact the victim.

In August 2025, another victim was identified by police. She told police she met Ans through Tinder and had gone for a drink with him before they went back to her address, where he raped her.

‌



Ans was further arrested in relation to the third victim and was charged and remanded.

During the examination of Ans' phone, DC Ferguson found messages between Ans and his first victim, who was then identified and confirmed that she had also been raped by Ans.

He was then charged with these offences as well, and the cases of all three victims were joined.

‌



During sentencing, the court heard from all three women raped by Ans.

The first victim said: "I'm finding it hard to describe the initial impact of Ans' rape. After the violent event occurred, it felt like I had to burn everything that made up the woman I was, so that then it would have happened to her rather than me.

"I rarely slept, and when I did, nightmares accompanied me. My anxiety was through the roof, supplemented by intrusive thoughts, intense nausea, and debilitating panic attacks.

‌



"Ans clearly saw the pain he had inflicted on me and then went on to hurt others in the same way. I truly believe that he is a dangerous and predatory man. No sentence can undo the damage he has caused or the years I will continue to live with the consequences of his actions."

In a statement, the second victim said: "When I think about what Ans did to me; him raping me started a chain of events that have led to some of the darkest and most difficult times that I have faced in my life.

"I still feel an intense amount of anger and rage towards him. I had told him 'NO', and I had pushed his hands away and pulled my leggings back up. My words meant nothing to him, and I now recognise that he had already decided what was going to happen to me, regardless of whether I consented to it or not.

‌



"People think that a rapist is someone hiding down an alley, or in a bush with a knife, that will drag you away and force themselves on you... but Ans made me realise that a rapist can be charismatic, educated and can arrive with a smile.

"Regardless of how he portrayed himself to me and others he is nothing but a rapist monster. He is a disgusting human being, and I hate him with every part of me."

The third victim said: "In terms of the physical impact, it took me many weeks before I was able to sleep properly again. Even now, I continue to experience nightmares and flashbacks relating to what happened. I became scared to be at home on my own in-case he showed up, my own home felt wrong and unsafe.

‌



"Psychologically, the impact of these events has affected almost every aspect of my life. I have suffered from severe anxiety and panic attacks as a result of my experience with Ans.

"The events have significantly affected my ability to trust others, particularly men. I find it difficult to form new relationships now as a result. As a girl who just wanted her happy ending, I feel I have paid a high price for trying to find it.

"I see Ans as directly responsible for my current symptoms and state of mind. If I hadn't met him and he hadn't done these things to me, I believe that I would be in a very different position now in my life. I feel that he is a risk to women, and that he used me sexually despite me making my boundaries clear."

‌



Sentencing, Judge Matthew Turner KC said each victim was in "a vulnerable position" in their lives at the time of Ans' horrific crimes. He added that the woman initially found Ans charming, but he preyed upon that to rape them and satisfy his own sexual desires.

Judge Turner said that Ans's lack of recognition of his criminality was "deeply troubling", adding that there was a complete disconnect between how he viewed his actions and the "single-minded pursuit of your own sexual gratification". Ans will also be required to sign the sex offenders register for life.

DC Ferguson said evidence in the case "clearly showed" that Ans had "made the same types of comments and offers towards each victim after raping them."

‌



He added: "This included apologising to them, telling them that it was a mistake, and that people make mistakes when first meeting, as well as offers of giving certain victims money and to take them shopping.

"In relation to one of the victims, it was also explained that he had offered to pay her $3,000 in compensation if she would 'leave it'. This victim refused his offer and had screenshot the messages he had sent, and sent these on as part of her evidence.

"Ans is a sexual predator who targeted these women on dating sites with the sole purpose of meeting up with them for sex. His motivation was clear. These women were looking for meaningful relationships, and were not seeking casual sexual encounters, and they made this clear to Ans.

Article continues below

"Despite this Ans created situations where they were each caused to be alone with him, and he then proceeded to rape them, and forced them into depraved sexual acts. Ans was driven by his sexual appetite, and the voices of his victims did not matter to him. He chose what was going to happen, and he forced his will onto others.

"Their clear boundaries and lack of consent did not matter to him."

DC Ferguson said the victims displayed "tremendous courage and strength" by giving evidence and that Devon and Cornwall Police would remain committed to "supporting women and girls who are victims of violence, and those persons who have been the victim of sexual offences."

News.title: Boy, 1, boiled alive in blistering hot bath after mum and boyfriend abandoned him
News.content:
Boy, 1, boiled alive in blistering hot bath after mum and boyfriend abandoned him

WARNING DISTRESSING CONTENT: Samantha Garver, 26, and her boyfriend Sergio Mena, 34, have been jailed forllowing the horriffic death of Garver's 1-year-old son Henry Wheatley-Brown in California

View 4 Images Henry Wheatley-Brown, 1, died in agony (Image: ABC7)

A California couple have been sentenced to more than a decade behind bars for the brutal murder of a 1-year-old.

‌



Samantha Garver, 26, and her boyfriend Sergio Mena, 34, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and child abuse causing great bodily injury to her 1-year-old son, Henry Wheatley-Brown.

‌



Little Henry died in horrific circumstances while in Mena’s care at the couple's home near in Sugarloaf, near Big Bear City, California on September 30, 2023.

‌



Wheatley-Brown died from severe burns after Mena put the toddler in a "scalding" hot bath and abandoned him, allegedly to pick up methamphetamine.

Following an investigation authorities said the boy was the victim of ongoing abuse after suffering second- and third-degree burns on his body as well as bodily bruising and several healing fractures in both arms.

View 4 Images The 1-year-old suffered terrible injuries (Image: ABC7)

‌



Child services also concluded following an investigation that the cause of the toddler's death was "abuse or neglect,” The Daily Express US reports.

Upon returning to the house Mena found the little boy screaming in agony after getting "severely burned" in the bath, according to the San Bernardino County District Attorney's Office. However, he made no effort to help relieve the boy's pain, prosecutors allege.

"Despite Henry's extensive and life-threatening injuries, neither defendant sought medical care, instead attempting to treat the burns with over‑the‑counter ointment," prosecutors said.

‌



It wasn't until the following day that the couple alerted authorities to his "shallow breathing." The district attorney's office said, "Paramedics found Henry without a pulse, ice‑cold to the touch and severely dehydrated."

View 4 Images Sergio Mena, 34, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and child abuse causing great bodily injury while Samantha Garver, 36, was convicted of manslaughter and child abuse causing great bodily injury (Image: ABC7)

The district attorney's office said in a statement, "Although nothing can bring back baby Henry or erase the suffering he endured, today's sentences deliver justice and ensure these defendants will never again harm a child. The San Bernardino County District Attorney's Office will honour Henry's memory by never forgetting him and by continuing to fight for vulnerable children."

‌



Sergio Mena, will spend 21 years behind bars while Samantha Garver will spend 14 years in jail.

There are years' worth of records documenting the alleged abuse that the little boy and his three older siblings suffered, which led to the San Bernardino County Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS) getting involved with Garber, according to The Los Angeles Times.

View 4 Images Samantha Garver will spend 14 years behind bars (Image: ABC7)

‌



The mother allegedly told staff at DCFS that she "felt like putting a pillow over" one of her children to stop their relentless crying, and posted a question on Facebook inquiring whether "duct taping a child's mouth is abusive."

The perplexing case led investigators to have differing views on the situation, with some saying the children faced "high risk" of abuse while another argued the children were "safe."

The child's own family members seemed to dismiss the severity of the child abuse occurring at home. The boy's grandmother, Sierra Rivers, appeared to argue that abuse is commonplace, acceptable, and can be overcome.

Article continues below

"I got abused as a kid, and I got hit as a baby, and I turned out fine," Rivers told The Los Angeles Times.

News.title: Suffolk wildfire still growing and unpredictable, says fire service
News.content:
Homes and a holiday caravan park were evacuated after the fire broke out and there are fears for rare birds and wildlife whose home is the heath and nearby RSPB Minsmere.

The "large-scale, wind-driven" fire was declared a major incident on Thursday morning, due to the size and complexity of the blaze which was helped by south-westerly winds.

On Thursday evening, Suffolk's chief fire officer, Jon Lacey, said: "Eighteen fire engines and 120 firefighters are involved in the response, but difficult terrain and limited access routes are making it hard for crews to reach some areas of the wildfire."

He confirmed approximately 100 to 150 people had been evacuated from their accommodation.

An update on the fire service's website said it was being supported by firefighters from neighbouring brigades, with engines also being sent from London.

"We have also requested additional national support, including wildfire specialist appliances, officers, and tactical advisers," it said.

"Around 50 people have received support through the rest centre, which remains open.

"We expect the response to continue for at least the next 48 hours."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to give the fire service "all the support it needs" to tackle the "very serious" heathland blaze.

Communities Secretary Angela Rayner praised firefighters for their "skill and dedication and bravery".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has called for Burnham to host an emergency Cobra meeting to discuss the outbreak of wildfires in Britain, including in Suffolk.

News.title: Andy Burnham to give regional mayors share of income tax
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will give all mayors of city regions in England a share of income tax revenue for the first time, as part of his drive to transfer power from Westminster to local leaders.

Burnham will also allow mayors of English strategic authorities to keep some cash from business rates collected in their areas, and gain greater control over services such as housing, transport, skills.

The government has not yet decided the exact portion of taxes mayors will be given, with more details to be announced when Chancellor John Healey delivers his first budget in the autumn.

Critics said the plans lacked detail and could lead to areas with weaker economies losing out on funding.

But Burnham said the move would "make good" on his pledge to "bring power home" to "every postcode in the country".

"Under our plans, more of the taxes raised in a community will stay in that community," the prime minister added.

The power to raise and control tax revenues is highly centralised in the UK, making the country an outlier by international standards.

The share of national taxes collected at a local level in the UK is 5.8%, the lowest in the G7, according to the OECD, external, a global policy forum.

That share is far below that of other countries with large economies such as France (20.4%), Japan (36%), and the US (45.7%).

As it stands, mayors of strategic authorities in England receive most of their funding from central government grants.

During his time as Greater Manchester mayor, Burnham pushed for greater control over tax revenue, rather than having to rely on government grants.

The UK government had already been exploring whether a share of revenue from national taxes could be distributed to metro mayors, before Burnham became prime minister earlier this month.

But in a major speech on devolution in June, Burnham said he would "oversee the biggest rebalancing of power our country has ever seen" if he became prime minister.

Burnham has put devolution at the heart of his plan for government, arguing that metro mayors are best placed to boost economic growth across the country.

News.title: Renowned ex-Royal Marine Nirmal Purja among 10 climbers feared missing after avalanche
News.content:
A ten-member international mountaineering team led by renowned Nepal-born former Royal Marine Nirmal Purja is feared missing after an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak, one of the world's highest mountains.

Pakistani mountaineering officials say the avalanche hit at around midday on Thursday on the 8,047-metre (26,400 ft) peak in the Karakoram range. There has been no subsequent communication with the team.

An American, a Chinese national, an Omani and five Nepalis are said to be part of the climbing group. Purja, the expedition leader, is known for climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre plus mountains in just over six months in 2019.

Searchers hope to use a helicopter if weather permits.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for expeditions, and is ranked as the world's 12th highest peak.

The Alpine Club of Pakistan released a statement saying it had been "in constant contact" with government authorities to launch "an immediate search and rescue operation".

The group said "every possible effort" was being made to ensure helicopter support and "all available resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity".

"The Club prays for the safety and successful rescue of all the climbers and stands in solidarity with their families and the international mountaineering community during this difficult time," it added.

Purja joined the British Army in 2003 and became a Royal Marine in 2009.

His climbing career began when he walked to Everest base camp in 2012 and, instead of returning as planned, decided to climb the entire mountain.
