Sports.title: Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close

Manchester United made an enquiry for Paraguay goalkeeper Orlando Gill, who starred at the World Cup, according to the player's agent - though a move to San Lorenzo now appears more likely for the Red Devils target

View 2 Images Orlando Gill is on the move after an impressive World Cup with Paraguay (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

World Cup star Orlando Gill was the subject of an enquiry from Manchester United, according to the player's representative, Mario Jara. The goalkeeper impressed for Paraguay as the South American nation faced the likes of France and upset Germany during the tournament.

‌



Gill is set to leave San Lorenzo this summer following his exploits, and United were among the candidates linked with his signature. Now, Jara has confirmed that the Red Devils reached out, though they no longer appear to be in the running.

‌



Senne Lammens established himself as United's first-choice keeper last season, and Michael Carrick has added Karl Darlow to his options from Leeds United. The former Newcastle shotstopper's arrival means it's unlikely another goalkeeper will arrive this summer.

‌



Nevertheless, Jara has confirmed he has held discussions with clubs in both England and Germany. The agent has indicated that the Gill is set to move imminently.

He told DSports Radio: "We are in talks with English clubs as well as clubs in Germany. There were enquiries with Manchester United.

Marcus Rashford posts Barcelona farewell message as dream return goes up in smoke READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to offload quartet including player they refused to swap for Carlos Baleba READ MORE :

"We only received two concrete offers. We are currently in the negotiation phase.

‌



"The sale is close, the time is right. We have to handle it very carefully because there are many things involved. It's ideal for him to take a step up in quality. He's prepared and capable of playing in any league, without a doubt."

He added: "We're trying to finalise it as quickly as possible for everyone's benefit. It would be very important for San Lorenzo; hopefully, it will come to fruition."

View 2 Images Orlando Gill was linked with a move to Manchester United this summer (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United are more likely to see goalkeepers leave the club. Andre Onana has already departed on loan to Trabzonspor, while Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek could both find new sides.

Vitek has featured in each of the Red Devils' friendlies so far, against Wrexham and Rosenborg, with Lammens only arriving back to Carrington on Thursday. Former Bristol City loanee is determined to find first-team action.

‌



"I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to be, hopefully, number one, so we will see. We will see what is going to happen," Vitek said after facing Wrexham.

"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so. I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete.

"I am ready for both, to be fair. [It] Depends what the club wants and also depends on the options. We will see.

Article continues below

"There have been a few interests on the table. But we hope to get the best one and hopefully it will happen soon."

Sports.title: 'Gianni Infantino should resign from FIFA now — or football will suffer forever'
Sports.content:
'Gianni Infantino should resign from FIFA now — or football will suffer forever'

Gianni Infantino, the president of FIFA since 2016, was on Thursday accused of "putting profit ahead of fans" amid the controversial plans to sell stakes of the World Cup

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino has become a danger to the game he was elected to protect. His proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors would reduce football’s greatest tournament to a financial asset, carved up by people interested in profit rather than passion. England will not take part. Neither will France, Germany, Spain, Italy or Europe’s other leading nations. They are right to threaten a boycott and must stand firm. Without Europe, the World Cup would be a sham: a gutted tournament missing many of its greatest teams, rivalries and supporters. Infantino knows this, yet he has still offered national associations £30 million to back his scheme. That is no way to run world football. It is an attempt to buy compliance while selling off the game’s crown jewels. The Mirror says Infantino has forfeited the right to lead FIFA. He should resign now. If he will not, he must be removed before his greed leaves football permanently poorer.

‌



Fires no freak

For weeks, Britain has watched in horror as wildfires tore through Europe. Now our own countryside is alight. More than 100 firefighters are battling flames across Suffolk heathland covering an area the size of 140 football pitches, while families have been forced from caravans and holiday parks. Their courage is extraordinary, as is the kindness of neighbours opening their homes to evacuees and their pets. Yet this cannot be dismissed as a freak disaster. We are heating the planet, drying the land and creating the conditions in which fires spread faster and burn harder. Andy Burnham must give crews every resource they need. But, despite the deniers, we all must act on the climate crisis with the urgency it demands. Europe’s nightmare is reaching our shores. Without change, this terrifying summer will become the new normal.

Ace in the old

At 100, Ivor Parker has finally turned a lifelong poker hobby into a job. After 86 years at the tables, he has been signed as the world’s oldest paid professional. His secret is patience, nerve and knowing when to hold ’em. Retirement, clearly, was never really on the cards.

Sports.title: Arne Slot immediately lined up for new job after Eddie Howe's bombshell Newcastle exit
Sports.content:
Arne Slot immediately lined up for new job after Eddie Howe's bombshell Newcastle exit

Arne Slot remains unemployed following his exit from Liverpool, but the Dutchman is now reportedly in the frame for a new job after developments involving Eddie Howe

View 2 Images Arne Slot is one of the contenders for the Al-Ahli job (Image: Getty Images)

Arne Slot could benefit from Eddie Howe's departure at Newcastle after the former Liverpool boss was reportedly shortlisted for the Al-Ahli job.

‌



Howe has walked away from Newcastle after five years in charge and the Magpies have already lined up his replacement. Newcastle have identified Al-Ahli manager Matthias Jaissle as the man to step into Howe's shoes on Tyneside ahead of the 2026/27 season.

‌



The club have been working on a succession plan for the past few weeks, with discontent growing behind the scenes. And the fact they are owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund - who also own Al-Ahli - has seen Jaissle in position to move to the Premier League.

‌



Slot has been in talks to succeed Ronald Koeman as the next Netherlands boss. But he could move to Saudi Arabia instead, with talkSPORT reporting that Slot is a candidate to replace Jaissle at Al-Ahli.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest caught out as Premier League gambling ban bites READ MORE :

Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure READ MORE :

Slot was sacked by Liverpool in May following the conclusion of a disappointing season campaign at the club. He was approached by Fulham over succeeding Marco Silva, but rejected the opportunity, with Alvaro Arbeloa eventually taking the job instead.

‌



Former Wolves and Nottingham Forest boss Vitor Pereira is also a contender for the Al-Ahli role. He has experience in Saudi Arabia, having spent 10 months at Al Shabab, while he also previously managed Al Ahli in 2013.

The 58-year-old is available following a brief spell at Forest, where he lasted just 20 games and was replaced by ex-Crystal Palace boss Oliver Glasner this summer.

Whoever does take the job will have big shoes to fill, with Jaissle having won 92 of his 138 games in charge and won back-to-back Asian Champions League titles.

‌



View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle is leaving Al-Ahli for Newcastle (Image: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty Images)

Slot emerged as the main contender to replace Koeman after the World Cup. However, talks with the KNVB have stalled over the terms with Slot reportedly keen to only sign a deal until the end of the 2028 Euros, rather than until 2030.

If he does take the Netherlands job, then Slot would be following in the footsteps of his predecessor at Liverpool, Jurgen Klopp, who has taken the Germany role. Like the Netherlands, Germany changed head coach following a disappointing campaign at the World Cup.

Article continues below

Slot has been succeeded by Andoni Iraola at Liverpool, with the Spaniard having stepped up after three impressive campaigns at Bournemouth.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino in trouble as new statement released after UEFA fury over World Cup plans
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino in trouble as new statement released after UEFA fury over World Cup plans

FIFA's controversial plans that would affect the World Cup have been met with anger from the football community, with CONCACAF joining UEFA in issuing a statement

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plans have been slammed (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

CONCACAF have rejected Gianni Infantino's plans to sell parts of the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. Their opposition to the plan proceeds UEFA's statement which pledged to boycott all FIFA competitions until the idea was dead in the water.

‌



Earlier this week, plans emerged that saw FIFA announce their intention to sell shares in its competitions, including the World Cup, which just took place in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Leading organisations within the sport have criticised the plans, with the FA supporting a recent statement issued by UEFA.

‌



After UEFA held a meeting in response to controversial proposals put forward by FIFA president Gianni Infantino that would see private investment introduced, CONCACAF, which makes up the nations in North and Central America including the USA and Canada, also converged their member nations to discuss the pitch.

‌



Gianni Infantino MUST GO - FIFA chief has no way back after brutal response to World Cup plot READ MORE :

UEFA statement in FULL as they boycott World Cup until FIFA abandon controversial proposal READ MORE :

They outlined their position in a statement which read: "Concacaf is a confederation united by the love of our game, where football comes first. Guided by this philosophy over the past ten years we have built, from the ground up, an organization founded on service, transparent governance, and the long-term stewardship of football.

"History has shown FIFA and the football family what happens when the custodians of the game lose sight of these values. With this in mind, Concacaf today convened a meeting of the presidents of its 41 Member Associations, together with its President, Council members, and its FIFA Council members, to discuss a proposal developed and presented by the FIFA President to establish ‘FIFA Forward Enterprise’ and sell interests in the FIFA World Cup to private investors.

"During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies. In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned. The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance. For these reasons, Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations have: Rejected the proposal.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Tasked their FIFA Council Members with engaging FIFA to determine how existing vast FIFA reserves could be used to increase FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region; and tasked their FIFA Council Members with instructing the FIFA President to ensure that any matter follows the proper governance processes via staff and FIFA Council, in accordance with the FIFA Statutes. Through these actions, Concacaf reaffirms that football's future—and its greatest asset—must remain in the hands of our football family."

UEFA released their own statement in response to the controversial plans, making their position clear that they will not participate in FIFA competitions as long as the proposals remain in play. The statement read: “UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions. UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

‌



“The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plans have been met with fury by UEFA members (Image: AFP or licensors)

“It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

‌



“National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. But our opposition goes far beyond process.

“The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

“This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

‌



“As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

“Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination. There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

Article continues below

“Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

Sports.title: Fowler, Cantlay impress as Malnati leads after threatening 59 round
Sports.content:
Rickie Fowler and Patrick Cantlay are in contention after the first round of the Rocket Classic in Detroit as leader Peter Malnati threatened a sensational sub-60 score.

Malnati shot a career-best nine-under 61 to tie the tournament's record for the first round to take a two-shot lead over Fowler and Ryan Gerard, with Cantlay and Patrick Fishburn another shot back.

When Malnati stood on the first tee, his caddie suggested leaving the driver in his bag to play it safe and set up a solid start.

Malnati, though, went against the advice and used his driver to put a tee shot in the middle of the fairway that set up his first of seven birdies on the front nine.

"Even in the beginning before I knew it was going to be a special day, I didn't feel the same level of like anxiety," he said.

"I don't think I took advantage of a super easy course. I played great."

Image: Peter Malnati hits from the 18th tee during the first round of the Rocket Classic (AP Photo/Jose Juarez)

With thoughts of a sub-60 round crossing his mind, he made a 55-foot putt for birdie at the 11th and was nine under through 13 holes before missing some putts down the stretch in a bogey-free round.

Detroit Golf Club underwent a $16 million renovation, including converting a couple of par-5 holes into par-4s and adding a lot of bunkers, in an attempt to restore Donald Ross' vision for it more than a century ago, while making it more challenging.

Fowler and Ryan Gerard shot 63s, putting them two shots back and one stroke ahead of Cantlay and Fishburn.

Michael Brennan surged up the leaderboard after starting two over through four holes with eight straight birdies - one shy of the PGA Tour record.

He finished with a 65, putting him four strokes back with a pack of players that includes Keegan Bradley, who appeared to be mocked by some spectators who pretended he hit a hole in one on the par-three fifth.

Open runner-up Cameron Young has work to do on one under while US Open champion Wyndham Clark is on one over.

Despite significant changes at the course, Malnati and many other players still went low at a tournament that has been a birdie fest since 2019, when a Detroit-based mortgage company ended a decade-long drought in Michigan without a PGA Tour stop that dated to Tiger Woods winning the last Buick Open.

The PGA Tour is moving to a new model for 2028, effectively creating two tours, and Detroit organizers are taking an exit. The Rocket Classic wasn't interested in continuing to spend $15 million a year to be part of the second tier and didn't want to double the costs to be part of the elite tier.

"It's definitely been a bummer to kind of come into this knowing it was the last one," said Fowler, a Rocket Mortgage spokesman and the tournament's 2023 champion.

Sports.title: Huddersfield beat Hull FC in bottom-of-the-table clash
Sports.content:
Super League: Huddersfield Giants beat Hull FC 22-16 in bottom of the table clash for second straight win

Huddersfield Giants beat Hull FC in a crucial match between the two sides at the bottom of the Super League (Allan McKenzie/SWpix.com)

Huddersfield twice came from behind and produced a second-half fightback as they picked up a second straight Betfred Super League victory with a 22-16 win over Hull FC at the Accu Stadium.

Following their win over York last week, Huddersfield registered back-to-back victories for the first time since April. They remain rock-bottom of the table but are now just two points behind losers Hull.

Huddersfield were on the front foot after being given a fresh set of six around 40 metres out and they made Hull pay after an inside ball from Harry Rushton was given to Chris Patolo who reached out across the whitewash. George Flanagan converted.

Hull managed to get themselves on level terms midway through the first half, Jake Arthur delivered a short ball to Joe Batchelor who was able to race clear and slide over.

The visitors took the lead just six minutes later following an excellent break by Cade Cust who had Ethan O'Neill and Davy Litten for support, and he was able to finish off in the corner but Zak Hardaker was unable to add the extras.

Huddersfield almost had their second try before the break but Jacob Gagai was unable to dot down in the corner and was denied a try following a video review.

Much like the first half, the hosts made a strong start to the second and had the opening try of the period, Tui Lolohea's kick forced a Hull knock-on and Connor Wrench was able to kick through before grounding behind the sticks.

Huddersfield's George Flanagan played a key role to help his side to victory (Picture by Allan McKenzie/SWpix.com)

Their lead was short-lived though, as Hull turned defence into attack with a break down the field courtesy of O'Neill and he offloaded to Litten who finished off the move to make it 16-12.

Huddersfield bit back once again when Lewis Jagger dived over to make it a level game and after Hull were pulled for a high tackle, the home side went down the other end and got the winning try when Flanagan dived behind the posts to pick up another vital win.

"It was nice to have a bit of belief at the back end of the game and find a way to win instead of lose," Huddersfield head coach Jim Lenihan told Sky Sports.

"It's the reward of a lot of hard work in training. The biggest part is we are looking forward to playing football. This is a very proud club that works hard behind the scenes, we want to walk round with some pride about ourselves."

Sports.title: England fight back to reach netball semi-finals at Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
England fought back to beat South Africa 58-54 to reach the netball semi-finals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Both sides needed to win to book a spot in the last four and England roared back from an early 17-11 deficit after the first quarter to keep their hopes of a second Commonwealth gold alive.

The Vitality Roses will face New Zealand in the second of Saturday's semi-finals after Australia play Jamaica, then the gold and bronze-medal matches take place on Sunday.

"Shout out to Halimat Adio. She was unreal in that second quarter. So proud of her to bring us that energy and get us back in the game when we needed it," captain Francesca Williams told TNT Sports.

"We have been under pressure all week to perform so for us to finish out a game like that and ride the wave of goal for goal in the last quarter and come out on top, I'm so proud."

Image: Halimat Adio player a pivotal role for England to slow down South Africa's Elmere van der Berg (PA)

England got off to a nervy start as South Africa goal shooter Elmere van der Berg came flying out of the blocks with 16 goals from 19 attempts which silenced the crowd at the OVO Hydro.

Halimat Adio and Funmi Fadoju came on, which tightened up England's defence, and it changed the momentum of the match as they slowly got themselves back into the contest to trail just 29-28 at half-time.

England went on a charge early in the third quarter with five consecutive goals to move 35-30 ahead and took a 45-41 lead into the last quarter.

Image: The Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh attended the match (PA)

As the clock ran down, England calmly maintained their slender four-goal advantage as Olivia Tchine and Lois Pearson kept their composure up front to get Anna Stembridge's side over the line.

Stembridge stepped up to become head coach just four months before the Commonwealth Games after Jess Thirlby resigned.

Netball has been in the Commonwealth Games since 1998 but England have never won a medal when it has been held in the United Kingdom.

Sports.title: Gomez to miss start of season - but will it impact Liverpool's transfer plans?
Sports.content:
Joe Gomez is expected to miss the start of Liverpool's Premier League campaign through injury - but it is not likely to impact the Reds' transfer plans.

The defender was forced off early in the first half of Liverpool's friendly with Sunderland in Nashville last weekend due to a muscle problem.

New Reds boss Andoni Iraola refused to put an exact timescale on Gomez's return but ruled him out of being back in time to face Newcastle on August 23, live on Sky Sports.

"Joe has a muscle injury. I think it was quite clear since he complained straight away, so it will depend how he evolves, but he will be some weeks off," Iraola said.

Asked for further detail on how long he expects to be without Gomez, the Liverpool head coach added: "It's a muscle injury and [with] muscle injuries it is difficult to say one day, but normally I always put myself as one month.

"If it goes very good the injury is a little bit less, if [not] it goes a little more. It's not massive, it's a normal muscle injury, [but] I think it's going to be impossible to have him for the start of the season because we are not so far [away]. It shouldn't be a lot more."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the best bits from Andoni Iraola's first Liverpool press conference in early July

Gomez injury will not affect Liverpool transfer plans

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Vinny O'Connor:

Liverpool's transfer plans remain unaffected by Gomez's injury despite the lack of options currently available to Iraola.

Their current priority is bringing in a wide forward - not a central defender - with Liverpool set to make a formal approach to PSG for Bradley Barcola.

Gomez's injury is viewed as short-term, with Iraola anticipating he will not miss much more than their opening game against Newcastle.

Virgil van Dijk returns from his post-World Cup break this week and will report to Liverpool's training base rather than travelling to the United States.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains the four things Liverpool fans should know about transfer target Bradley Barcola

Giovanni Leoni is still rehabbing from an ACL injury he suffered early last season, while new signing Jeremey Jacquet is preparing to play his first game of pre-season against Leeds on Sunday after a long lay-off with a shoulder problem.

Liverpool could realistically go into the start of the new season with only Van Dijk and Jacquet as their available senior options at centre-back.

Iraola admitted in Thursday's press conference that Liverpool are currently thin on options at the back, but was positive about the performances of youngsters Luke Chambers, Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Talla Ndiaye, who have stepped in during pre-season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky News' city editor Mark Kleinman provides the latest update as Amit Bhatia's syndicate - which could include Jeff Bezos - line up a bid for a minority stake in Liverpool

"You have seen these games, we are pretty thin in the centre-back position," he said. "We still don't have Virgil. The only real centre-backs we have right now are Mor and Ify, who are 18 years old, just arrived to the club and they are doing incredibly well.

"On Wednesday, Luke Chambers played there. He is not a centre-back but he played really well. We have to until we recover some bodies.

"I think Jeremy is ready to go and we will recover Virgil, but I'm happy that playing against Sunderland, against Wrexham, good teams with 18-year-old centre-backs, the team has showed composure and solidity at the back and [that] speaks very well about them."

PSG closer to agreeing deal former Liverpool target Akliouche

Latest from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas:

PSG are getting closer to agreeing a deal with Monaco for Maghnes Akliouche. Negotiations are in the advanced stages.

The winger market is starting to move, with Yan Diomande moving closer to Real Madrid and Liverpool preparing to bid for Barcola.

Liverpool also made initial contact with Monaco about Akliouche - but a move for Barcola is anticipated since Sky Sports News broke that news on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Diamond Necklace sparkles in Nassau Stakes
Sports.content:
Diamond Necklace lived up to her billing when extending her unbeaten record with a dominant display in the Qatar Nassau Stakes at Goodwood.

Having rounded off a perfect juvenile campaign with victory in the Prix Marcel Boussac on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp, Aidan O'Brien's filly has returned to France to secure back-to-back Classic wins this year, in the French 1000 Guineas and French Oaks.

She was the 4-6 favourite to make it six from six as she faced her elders for the first time and while Friendly Soul did her best to shake her off, Ryan Moore always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard Diamond Necklace and she pulled two and three-quarter lengths clear with the minimum of fuss.

An impressed Moore said: "That's the best she's felt, she's improving with her racing. Aidan said she was up in her weight a bit today so she's obviously thriving.

"She's classy, it was very easy really. She travelled smoothly and quickened up well, she's a little bit idle in front still, but she's a proper racing machine.

"She gives you a classy feel, every time I've ridden her she's travelled with loads of pace, loads of enthusiasm and she has a turn of foot; that's what her father (St Mark's Basilica) had, a real good turn of foot and that's what's evident with her."

O'Brien was delighted to see Diamond Necklace enhance her unbeaten record and said: "She's lovely and she's progressing and she was heavier today, but Rachel (Richardson, work rider) was confident that was just strength she was building rather than just being heavy and it was the way she went through the line.

"There's a lot of people around her who help her and she's a lovely filly. This was a mile and a quarter against older fillies and we didn't know what was going to happen. We put in a lot of pace as we didn't want a Mickey Mouse race and she has options now.

"You can see her quality the way she travels through a race and Ryan was hoping they would lead him longer and he just had to go on as her stride was getting broken. She is a great cruiser and she has a lot of quality and is progressing great so I'm over the moon."

Diamond Necklace was shortened to 8-1 from 14s for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe by Paddy Power, but O'Brien is yet to commit on stretching her stamina any further than the 10 furlongs, with the star filly holding a multitude of options for later in the season.

He added: "Constitution River is the boss and everyone has to fall into line behind him. At the moment he is going to York and we're looking forward to that.

"She could stay at a mile and a quarter and go to the race at Leopardstown (Irish Champion Stakes), or France for an Arc trial, she has all those races open to her and she does handle soft ground as well as she handles fast ground.

"The Arc is possibility and she could be a Breeders' Cup filly, it will depend how far we ask her to go. Her next run will tell us where she is going to go and she has a long stride on her and loves nice ground and a fast track, she has a lot of options."

Friendly Soul has endured her fair share of drama since returning from injury this year, being the horse who put a foot in a hole at Haydock before a luckless run in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot.

"She's run a fine race against a top class three-year-old who is unbeaten," said Thady Gosden, who trains the five-year-old alongside father John.

"It was a very good effort and we will now in consultation with George and Julia (Strawbridge, owners) look at the programme ahead in which there are some good opportunities for older fillies."

Enceladus impresses in Gordon - but Leger run not set in stone

Joseph O'Brien is keen to keep his options open with Enceladus following his authoritative victory in the Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

The Sea The Stars colt has looked much improved since being stepped up in trip this season, with a comeback win at Cork followed by Royal Ascot success in the King George V Stakes.

The William Haggas-trained pair of Desert Hero (2023) and Merchant (2025) won the same Ascot handicap in recent years before landing this Group Three prize and after being sent off a well-backed 6-4 favourite to follow suit, Enceladus finished strongly under Dylan Browne McMonagle, keeping Geryon at bay by a length and a quarter.

Classic sponsors Betfred make Enceladus a 10-1 shot from 25-1 for the Leger, a race which saw O'Brien break his British Classic duck as a trainer with Galileo Chrome six years ago - but the trainer warned he is not certain to head for Doncaster in September.

O'Brien was at Galway rather than Goodwood, from where he told Press Association: "I'm delighted, it was a nice ride from Dylan. It was a really nice performance and he's a progressive, improving colt.

"It was a big step up in class and it's a hard thing to do, but he's going the right way and I'm delighted to have a horse of his potential for Maria and the Niarchos team."

On a Leger bid, he added: "It is one of the more obvious options, but I don't know if we'll rush him past a mile and a half either. Let's see how he pulls up and let the dust settle and we'll lock in his next target after that."

Image: Dylan Browne McMonagle riding Enceladus to win the Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes during day three of the Qatar Goodwood Festival

McMonagle said: "He's a lovely, big, straightforward horse. He's done nothing but improve and each run he's getting better.

"I think he's going to be a very nice horse going forward and I do think he's up to that level (Group Twos and Group Ones) with a bit of time.

"As you can see he's still a big baby - when he's getting there he's just doing enough, but he was a good winner.

"He handles that ground well and I think he's got a bit of class - he's a horse to look forward to and one to keep an eye on."

Colin Keane said of the runner-up: "I thought for a few strides that we were going to get to Dylan's horse (Enceladus) but he picked up and went away again.

"I'd say the winner is smart but we're smart as well, he's just a bit of a work in progress. He probably didn't (see it out as well as the winner), but I do think in time he will.

"He's a little hard on himself, he wears earplugs to help him relax so he's a work in progress but a horse with a big future hopefully."
